newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's K&P to offer 55 mln new shares at HK$1 each.
newsitem.headline: HK's K&P to offer 55 mln new shares at HK$1 each.

text.p: Hong Kong electronics firm K & P International Holdings Ltd will offer 55 million new shares at HK$1 each, with one warrant to be issued for every five shares, a statement issued for the company said on Wednesday.
Application forms are available from December 12 to 17, while dealings in shares are expected to start on January 2, 1997, the statement said.
K & P makes conductive silicone rubber keypads and develops electronic calculators and alarm clocks and plastic products.

Net proceeds from the issue, estimated at HK$45 million, will be used to build a new factory in China, to acquire additional machinery for higher production capabilities and capacities, and to support the group's vertical diversification into the production of alarm clock movements.

The company forecasts profit after taxation but before exceptional and extraordinary items for full-year 1996 to be at least HK$32 million. Net profit stood at HK$11.41 million in the first half of this year, and HK$23.06 million in full-year 1995.
The issue price represents a price-earnings multiple of 5.19 on a weighted average basis and 6.57 on a proforma fully diluted basis, the statement said.
The issue is sponsored and managed by Lippo Securities Ltd.

The group expects growth on all business fronts, product range expansion and market expansion into new territories such as China, Singapore, Malaysia, the Middle East, Russia, Eastern Europe and South America, the statement said.
It did not name the manufacturer's existing markets, or give a timeframe for its expansion programme.
